$comment: flux-expr/2 extension vectors (EXPR-SPEC-2 §2, §3, §5, §11): previous versions, paths over several links, aggregates over children and windows over siblings, in the shape of expr-vectors.json (EXPR-SPEC §5). Each vector carries its text ('expr'), the side it is read for ('flux': a FLUX-side rule's text), the model fragment ('model_fragment', an entry of 'models') and expose it is checked against, and its position ('predicate': it must be bool; 'value': a derive's expr, with 'target' naming the derived column when there is one). 'expect.parse' is the syntax tree (EXPR-SPEC-2 §11), or the FLX code when the text does not parse; 'expect.check' is 'ok' or the code the check refuses it with; an accepted vector also gives its type, its static scale for a number (null is unbounded), its canonical text ('expect.unparse') and its values ('expect.eval'). An eval case names a dataset of 'data' and a row of the vector's expose (its 0-based position, as a string). No JSON number appears: a number is a decimal string, or 'p/q' for a rational with no finite decimal expansion, compared by value; a date is YYYY-MM-DD. A predicate's value is always true or false.
